title: Optimize UPDATE and DELETE RETURNING row preallocation
constraints: Preserve UPDATE, DELETE, filtering, index maintenance, and RETURNING semantics
rationale: UPDATE and DELETE collect candidate key-value pairs before evaluating filters and RETURNING. When RETURNING is present, the candidate count is a safe upper bound for the returned rows, so preallocating the row buffers reduces Vec growth during write workloads.
steps: Preallocate DELETE RETURNING rows from candidate key-value count
Preallocate UPDATE RETURNING rows from candidate key-value count
Leave non-RETURNING paths with empty row buffers
Verify UPDATE RETURNING, DELETE RETURNING, and no-match update behavior
expected_impact: Reduces allocation churn in UPDATE and DELETE RETURNING result collection without changing affected rows or returned values.
